executiveSummary.headline: Repository-Intelligence-Platform is a TypeScript repository with 21,376 lines of code in 29 modules, using Next.js and React.
overview: The analysis processed 197 of 202 code files (108 production, 94 test) out of 543 files in total. 100 percent of internal imports were resolved, which is the main reliability number for the dependency graph.
The 108 production files form a dependency graph with 303 edges and no circular dependencies.

Scores: Architecture 98 (high confidence), Maintainability 76 (high confidence), Security hygiene 86 (medium confidence), Testing and CI 100 (high confidence), Documentation 89 (high confidence), Maintenance activity 58 (high confidence).
strengths: No circular dependencies between files or modules.
Almost all internal imports resolve (100 percent), so graph conclusions are well supported.
18 architecture decision records document design choices.
No committed secrets were detected by the checks that ran.
A dependency lockfile pins exact versions.
concerns: 6 risky GitHub Actions settings found, for example unpinned actions.
5 files rank high on the risk index, the top one is packages/core/src/findings/generate.ts.
30 functions have high or very high complexity.
Go and Rust only received detection and line counts, so architecture conclusions do not cover it.
nextSteps: Pin 6 GitHub Actions to commit SHAs
Reduce risk in 5 high-risk files (simplify and add tests)

rules.description: Utilities must not depend on other layers
The intermediate representation is the stable core and may only use utilities
Detection may use utilities, the IR and acquisition types only
Report builders consume the report model and nothing else

limitations: Static analysis cannot recover runtime behavior, developer intent, or undocumented design decisions.
A report with no findings in an area does not prove that area is sound or secure.
Level 1: file detection and line counts only. No dependency, symbol or complexity analysis.
Dynamic imports and require calls with non-literal arguments are counted but not resolved.
Imports are resolved with the TypeScript module resolver over the repository snapshot. Packages that exist only in node_modules (not analyzed) are reported as external.
tsconfig extends targets outside the repository are ignored, so paths defined there are not applied.
Framework conventions (for example file-system routing) are not modeled.
Complexity counts decision points (if, loops, case, catch, ternary, logical and nullish operators) per function.

Import extraction is lexical (strings and comments are ignored) and is not a full Python parser.
Dynamic imports (importlib, __import__) are not detected.
Imports that match neither the standard library nor a repository package are assumed to be third-party packages.
Source roots are inferred from package layout (__init__.py), src and lib directories.
Complexity is an approximation from decision keywords, not an AST measurement.
Only top-level functions and classes are listed as symbols.
Dependencies between different languages (for example a web client calling an API) are not modeled. Each language is analyzed separately.

Risk index = weighted mean of available factors: complexity percentile (0.30), dependents percentile (0.25), change frequency percentile (0.25), lack of test linkage or coverage (0.20). At least 2 factors are required. It ranks files by how costly a change could be. It does not predict defects.
Languages with detection and line counts only (support level 1): go, rust.
File renames are not followed, so a renamed file starts a new history.
Squash merges attribute the whole change to the squasher, which can hide real authorship.
Author identity is the commit author name. The same person under different names is counted separately.
Churn and commit counts measure change activity, not quality or effort.
